scope: Bounded cross-jurisdiction discovery from Danish EU free-movement residence law and official guidance, carrying prior country-pack and taxonomy findings forward as search leads. Covers Portugal legal publication/version/reuse, Law 37/2006 and related EEA/Swiss/Andorra routes, general immigration and family procedures, forms, visas/missions, administrative procedure/remedies, public access, privacy, oversight, legal aid, civil-status evidence, and administrative case-law discovery. Portugal is an EU Member State. No legal equivalence or exhaustive inventory is asserted.
retrieval_status: The 19 October retrieval pass saved 46 exact responses; 19 converted review artifacts remain unaccepted and are being moved to the Monitor archive. As of 24 October, 61 official links are accepted within narrow scopes, three Gov.pt pages are not relied upon for current procedures, and four AIMA routes remain under human review. No local copies or topics are accepted.

comparison_seed.source: Danish EU free-movement residence law and official guidance
comparison_seed.relationship_note: Portugal Law 37/2006 has a close functional relationship to the Danish seed because it transposes Directive 2004/38 and regulates EU-citizen/family entry and residence. Its express EEA/Swiss provisions, Portuguese-national family extension, municipal registration, AIMA card route and separate Portugal-Andorra treaty must be preserved. The general Foreigners Act is only a partial match and serves distinct routes. No legal equivalence is asserted.

previous_findings_carried_forward: Prior Denmark, Sweden, Czechia, Hungary, Romania and other jurisdiction packs are search leads only; verify each Portugal candidate at its first-party publisher.
N-Lex is a national-law discovery lead, not a Portuguese publisher, complete source-class inventory or monitored legal record.
A documented data/API format, general open-data law or reuse notice does not by itself establish API registration requirements, endpoint access, unrestricted reuse, or conversion permission.
Keep EU, EEA EFTA, Swiss, Andorran, UK Withdrawal Agreement, Portuguese-family and general third-country routes distinct, even where operational guidance groups categories.
Consolidated texts, article change histories and legal-analysis pages aid discovery; DRE says they have no legal value, so preserve original acts, amendments, corrections and commencement.
Dynamic agency pages, portals, forms, fees, mission instructions and document checklists require current parent-page rediscovery.
Court and oversight databases may be selected; state dates, search filters and publication limits and do not infer absence from zero results.
